title: Distilling Sequential Computation in Transformer Language Models
summary: The method replaces multi-token spans in the prompt and stored KV cache entries with single surrogate embeddings produced by a lightweight merge module, applied to pretrained models without architectural changes or fine-tuning, using a rollback mechanism during decoding. It costs training and maintaining the merge module (plus optional lightweight adaptation for better trade-offs) and introduces some accuracy degradation that grows with the compression rate. It can fail on workloads where predictable-span assumptions break down, such as code, exact-copy retrieval, or numeric content, where merging tokens loses functionally critical information.
rationale: It fits a single 24 GB GPU and requires no model retraining, but the accuracy-compression trade-off must be validated on the reader's specific tasks before production use.
technique: On-the-fly token-span merging for prompt and KV cache compression
